parsed.explanation: The combined regime splits sharply. National entry is a universal exposure: the 2025 sex-at-birth passport/visa regime, the February 2025 cable directing refusal and potential lifetime fraud findings where documents 'cast doubt' on sex, documented passport confiscations stranding travellers, and allied governments issuing trans-specific advisories. Every trans visitor crosses that layer; consequences include refusal, stranding, and, if detained, a national corrections/immigration custody record featuring hormone removal, forced labour and sexual abuse. The state layer is materially protective: no facility ban, no bathroom offence, no minor-care ban, marriage recognised, sodomy repealed, vetoed hostile bills, a police department avoiding misgendering, though no statewide GI discrimination law and restricted local marker changes (resident-facing). Daily in-state exposure is friction, not custody.

entry_documents.exposure: Documented universal national exposure: passports issued only as M/F per sex assigned at birth; X markers stopped; visa cable instructs refusal where sex is doubted and considers lifetime fraud findings; travellers report confiscated passports and stranding; foreign advisories issued.
entry_documents.protection: X passports already issued remain valid to expiry; fraud finding requires four elements and is never automatic; litigation ongoing; legal-aid FAQ exists.
entry_documents.interaction: Entry screening is the first operative layer every visitor meets; a document mismatch can escalate from questioning to refusal or fraud allegation before state law ever applies.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: If detained, national corrections and immigration custody show hormone removal, forced 'conversion' practices, forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and sexual abuse of trans people; bathroom-trespass arrest precedent (elsewhere) shows handcuffing and men's-ward holding.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Visa fraud findings require all four elements with limited waivers; several orders enjoined; no documented visitor imprisonment for gender identity in this state.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A border discrepancy could route a visitor into national detention systems governed by the harshest documented rules; the state offers no custody protocol of its own.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal order bars gender-identity-congruent access in federally funded single-sex facilities; 4 states criminalise certain restroom use; this state has no such ban and no sex-definition law, so state/public-building access is unrestricted locally.
federal_state_facilities.protection: State executive order (2019) prohibits GI discrimination in state services and contracting; facility use per identity is lawful statewide per equality map.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Facility access depends on venue: state and local government buildings are safe; federal buildings and travel to other states re-engage hostile rules.

care_services.exposure: Two major hospital systems paused youth gender-affirming pharmacologic care (Jan 2026) under national funding pressure; national proposed rules bar public-insurance reimbursement for under-18 care; national subpoenaing of hospitals' youth records raises disclosure exposure.
care_services.protection: No state ban on youth care; governor vetoed ban and insurance exclusion; insurers barred from transgender-care exclusions; state joined multistate challenge.
care_services.interaction: A travelling minor's medication continuity is exposed to national payment rules even where state law permits care; adult emergency care not documented as restricted.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National framing treats trans issues as 'radical gender ideology'; counterterrorism strategy prioritises 'radically pro-transgender' groups; EO directs prosecution of teachers facilitating minor social transition; state legislatures repeatedly introduced restriction bills.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Governor publicly commits to vetoing unwelcoming bills and vetoed 2023/2024 bills; state repealed sodomy 1983; police department stopped listing victim gender to avoid misgendering.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: National hostile framing raises discovery probability at borders and schools; state law enforcement operates under a contrasting, largely neutral posture.

minors_guardians.exposure: Youth care paused at two hospital systems under national funding pressure; national orders framing minor transition as 'mutilation' and directing prosecution of facilitators; proposed insurance bar for under-18s.
minors_guardians.protection: State bans nothing for minors: no care ban (vetoed twice), no sports ban enacted, no facility ban; 2017 poll shows 73% support for GI-inclusive anti-discrimination law.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling minor faces little state-level restriction but inherits national care-access and school-speech exposure; guardians face no state liability.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No statewide GI hate-crime coverage (sexual orientation used as charging route, systematicity undocumented); 21% of population in cities with full GI ordinances; social conservatism nationally (66% support birth-sex documents).
street_violence_police_response.protection: 1982 statewide sexual-orientation public-accommodation ban; national hate-crime statute covers GI; several cities/counties prohibit GI discrimination; July 2026 assessment places state in low-risk group.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Street friction likely minor; recourse is patchwork — a visitor outside protected cities relies on national hate-crime law and local police practice.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No statewide GI anti-discrimination statute; licence marker change only in limited circumstances, birth certificate requires surgery, no X option, restrictive name change (resident-facing); equality-map profile dated May 2025.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Operative protections documented: 2019 executive order, municipal ordinances, hate-crime charging via sexual orientation, ongoing national litigation may relax passport rules.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Uncertainty centres on which national measures are enjoined at travel time and on border officer discretion; state-level unknowns are lighter.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar: Kestrel Isles' discretionary secondary screening with refusal-and-return outcomes mirrors the national document/cable regime here — humiliating, administrative, no custody. This jurisdiction adds a documented custody-abuse record if detention occurs, but its state layer is more protective than Kestrel's unmitigated exposure, netting slightly above.

Clear distinction: 0.35-A is a universal register with near-automatic exclusion and no remedy. Here the fraud finding requires four elements and is 'never automatic', X passports remain valid, litigation is active, and in-state life lacks any facility ban — materially less severe than a routine-exclusion regime.

Vellmaris shows brief detention corrected by working national equality law and a functional accountability board. This state lacks a statewide GI statute and its national layer has no reliable remedy at the border, but daily state-level exposure is comparable — friction, not punishment — placing it just below 0.65 overall.

Drellia's universal registration/database exposure reaches every visitor continuously. This jurisdiction's universal exposure is confined to entry screening and federal facilities; once inside, the state imposes no registration, facility ban or database flagging, so it sits clearly above 0.45.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime is two-layered. The national layer imposes a universal, unavoidable entry exposure — binary passport enforcement, sex-doubt refusals with potential lifetime fraud bars, scanner/pat-down outing risk, and a custody system documented to harm trans detainees — and it is the binding constraint on any traveller's journey. The state layer is genuinely benign by comparison: no facility or drag restrictions, no minor-care ban, repeated gubernatorial vetoes, marriage recognition, municipal protections covering a fifth of the population, and police practice avoiding misgendering. Daily in-state severity is friction and patchy recourse, not imprisonment; the catastrophic documented harms (custody abuse, conversion practices) trigger only if the national layer detains the traveller. Netting universal national exposure against a protective state yields a score just below the 0.65 tier, near 0.58.
